answer: An orchard of agents stays honest when each identity must tend its own tree: every identity periodically completes a unique sequential proof-of-work puzzle bound to its key, which cannot be parallelized or shared across clones. One operator spinning up thousands of fakes must pay the full compute cost for each, like harvesting nectar flower by flower instead of draining a hive at once, while identities that wander off or idle lose trust weight. Cost scales linearly with fakes, so sybils turn uneconomical before they can outvote real workers.
